title: Spark
tagline: The public record for ideas — show what you're building, who with, and how.
blurb: Versioned idea pages, executable context bundles, forks that carry lineage.
desc: People sit on ideas because sharing feels risky, and the thinking behind projects — the orchestration — lives on whiteboards and scattered docs with no public, versioned home. GitHub holds the artifacts; nobody holds the thinking.

Spark gives every idea a living page: description, demos, trials, team, and a decision log with timestamped, immutable history. Publishing openly becomes your receipt. Forks must carry lineage, so attribution is structural.

Why now: AI is making code the commodity output of ideas. The scarce upstream artifact is intent — prompts, instruction files, roadmaps, decisions. A Spark page packages that as an executable context bundle: fork it, clone it into an agent, and instantiate the project.

commits.msg: Decision log promoted to first-class element; orchestration-layer thesis
Context bundles: ideas as executable artifacts
Initial framework: vision, core objects, interactions, MVP scope
